report.summary: Observed: the astronomy-shop was freshly deployed at 16:08:47-16:08:48 (all pods created then, restartCount 0) and the postgresql pod ran a fresh initdb plus /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql at 16:08:55-16:08:56. Between 16:09:45 and 16:09:55 every PostgreSQL client workload received a new pod template (product-catalog revisions 2,3,4 including a switch of DB_CONNECTION_STRING to Secret product-catalog-db-conn, product-reviews revision 2, accounting revision 2 with an unchanged image digest), and ConfigMap postgresql-init shows a much later resourceVersion than every other configmap created the same second, i.e. it was edited after creation. Seconds later, from 16:09:57 onward, the running postgres rejected role otelu: 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' (scram-sha-256). product-catalog's and product-reviews' own spans carry that exact error, checkout fails preparing orders via product-catalog, frontend returns HTTP 500 on /api/product-reviews, /api/recommendations, /api/checkout and /api/products/{id}, and the load generator reported a 0.857 request failure ratio at 16:10:15. Postgres itself is Running/Ready and accepted connections (it rejects credentials, it is not down), cart/valkey calls succeeded, pods did not crash or OOM, and every flagd fault-injection flag is off. Hypothesis (not verifiable with readable data): a rotated DB credential was written to the client workloads and/or to ConfigMap postgresql-init but the live PostgreSQL role otelu kept the password from its 16:08:56 initdb run, so the clients and the database now disagree; the actual credential values in Secret product-catalog-db-conn and in the deployments' env are redacted, so which side deviates cannot be shown.

ConfigMap astronomy-shop/postgresql-init contains init.sql with the statement 'CREATE USER otelu WITH PASSWORD 'otelp_7k9m2q4x';' plus the accounting, reviews and catalog schemas/tables that product-catalog, product-reviews and accounting use.

Deployment product-catalog's pod template changed three times immediately before the failures: ReplicaSets product-catalog-6bc6bd6ff4 (revision 1, created 16:08:48Z, inline DB_CONNECTION_STRING value) and product-catalog-6d88bd6688 (revision 2, created 16:09:45Z, inline value), then product-catalog-556cd4f989 (revision 3) and product-catalog-6ff66f4b58 (revision 4, 1 ready replica) both created 16:09:48Z with DB_CONNECTION_STRING taken from secretKeyRef secret 'product-catalog-db-conn'; the image stayed ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-product-catalog in all of them.

The other PostgreSQL clients were also re-rolled in the same seconds with unchanged images: Deployment product-reviews got ReplicaSet product-reviews-7cdd9d8df7 (revision 2, created 16:09:55Z, 1 ready replica) replacing product-reviews-7bccd49cb7 (revision 1, 16:08:48Z), and Deployment accounting got ReplicaSet accounting-67495c6c98 (revision 2, created 16:09:52Z) replacing accounting-5897477844 (revision 1) with the identical image digest sha256:51e6720438c13d0a4fefd129b01e2422b176fdb18a9ea71ef08fd84e717e82f4, i.e. a configuration-only rollout.

product-catalog's own spans fail on its database: oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts returns rpc.grpc.status_code 13 with otel.status_description 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"', and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct returns code 5 'Product Not Found: L9ECAV7KIM' / 'Product Not Found: LS4PSXUNUM' (16:10:12-16:10:14).

product-reviews' own spans fail on its database connection: operation get_product_reviews throws psycopg2.OperationalError with message 'connection to server at "postgresql" (10.96.107.58), port 5432 failed: FATAL:  password authentication failed for user "otelu"' (spans at 16:10:07 and 16:10:13), and its oteldemo.ProductReviewService/GetProductReviews server spans carry the same exception in their logs.

checkout's own spans fail with the consequence of the product-catalog failure: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder returns rpc.grpc.status_code 13 with 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"66VCHSJNUP"' / '#"L9ECAV7KIM"' and its oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans return code 5, while its oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans in the same traces have rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

recommendation's own span get_product_list fails with grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError carrying 'failed to load products: failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' propagated from product-catalog, and frontend spans for the same traces return HTTP 500.

frontend returned HTTP 500 error spans (error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR) for /api/product-reviews/[productId]/index, /api/recommendations, /api/checkout and /api/products/[productId]/index across 16:09:49-16:10:14, with exception messages naming the postgres authentication failure and the failed order preparation.

All 27 pods in astronomy-shop are Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0, including postgresql-6bd9b846cb-24dtg, product-catalog-6ff66f4b58-9pgg6 and product-reviews-7cdd9d8df7-bkc85; every deployment reports 1/1 ready replicas.

cart is not part of this failure: cart's own spans for valkey-cart:6379 and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart completed, and the checkout client spans to CartService report rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in the failing checkout traces.

Rejected: pod crashes, OOMKills or evictions caused the service failures. All astronomy-shop pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, and the replaced product-catalog / product-reviews / accounting pods were controller rollouts (new ReplicaSets with restart count 0), not damaged pods.

Rejected: the 16:08:49-16:09:18 warnings in astronomy-shop (FailedMount 'failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for the condition', Readiness probe failed on grafana, Startup probe failed on opensearch-0, otel-collector-agent readiness 503, opensearch-pdb NoPods) explain the application errors. They occur during the initial start of those pods, before the credential change at 16:09:45-16:09:55, and none of them concerns a PostgreSQL client workload.

Most likely cause (unverifiable in detail because the credential values are redacted): a database-credential change was applied at 16:09:45-16:09:55 to the PostgreSQL client workloads - Deployment product-catalog switched DB_CONNECTION_STRING to Secret product-catalog-db-conn and was re-rolled 3 times, Deployment product-reviews and Deployment accounting were re-rolled with unchanged images - while the live role otelu in the running postgresql pod still enforces the password it received at initdb 16:08:56 from the earlier version of ConfigMap postgresql-init. The clients therefore present a credential the database rejects, which explains every downstream error; the fault originates in the credential configuration carried by these client workloads (and by the edited init ConfigMap), not in pod or database availability.

Alternative reading of the same evidence: ConfigMap postgresql-init was the object edited (resourceVersion 221688 versus ~220440 for its peers created at 16:08:47Z) and the change was meant as a rotation of the database credential, but the postgresql pod was not restarted or altered afterwards (single container instance, 0 restarts), so the live role password and the ConfigMap no longer describe the same credential; the client rollouts then adopted the ConfigMap's newer value. Under this reading the mismatch originates in the ConfigMap-authored credential that was never applied to the running database.

Recommendation (not executed): reconcile the PostgreSQL credential to one source of truth - verify the live role otelu's password against the value used by Secret product-catalog-db-conn and by the product-reviews and accounting env, then either ALTER USER otelu to the rotated secret value or restart postgresql so initdb re-applies ConfigMap postgresql-init, and confirm the 'FATAL: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' lines cease and product-catalog ListProducts / product-reviews GetProductReviews return data again.

gaps: Secret product-catalog-db-conn and the DB_CONNECTION_STRING password values in Deployments product-catalog, product-reviews and accounting are redacted, so I could not compare the clients' credential with the password the live PostgreSQL role otelu enforces; which side holds the wrong value is unverified.

The credential values as they stood before 16:09:45 are unknown: Kubernetes objects expose only current state and managedFields are stripped, so the pre-change DB_CONNECTION_STRING contents cannot be read.

The actor that patched Deployments product-catalog, product-reviews, accounting and ConfigMap postgresql-init at 16:09:45-16:09:56 is not visible in any log or event read (no ConfigMap/Secret events were recorded); change_history is not integrated in this Run.

Only one postgres container instance exists (no previous container logs) and the postgres pod was not restarted after initdb, so no ALTER ROLE or other postgres-side credential statement is visible in the logs.

accounting was re-rolled config-only at 16:09:52Z but I found no error evidence for it: its logs stopped at 16:09:55Z startup and a filtered error search returned no lines, so accounting's impact is unconfirmed (its DB_CONNECTION_STRING password is also redacted).

Prometheus has samples only from about 16:10:15Z in this run, so there is no pre-incident baseline for error or latency comparison; the span metric status_code label has only the value STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so per-service error rates are not measurable from metrics and traces are a sample only.

Services ad, currency, email, fraud-detection, payment, quote, shipping and the kafka/valkey backends beyond the cart spans were not checked for their own error signals, so they are neither confirmed affected nor confirmed healthy.
next_steps: Compare the password inside Secret product-catalog-db-conn (and the env values of product-reviews and accounting) with the live role password in PostgreSQL as a human with secret-read rights, to decide which side must be corrected.
Inspect PostgreSQL pg_authid / run a psql check as superuser (POSTGRES_USER=root) and, if the clients match ConfigMap postgresql-init, ALTER USER otelu to the rotated secret value.

Check whether a credential-rotation tool or operator patched the deployments and the init ConfigMap at 16:09:45-16:09:56 and make the rotation atomic (update DB role and all clients together, or restart postgresql after editing the init ConfigMap).
After alignment, verify that product-catalog ListProducts, product-reviews GetProductReviews and checkout PlaceOrder succeed and that the load generator failure ratio returns near zero.

CREATE USER otelu WITH PASSWORD 'otelp_7k9m2q4x';

-- Accounting Service: create a schema
CREATE SCHEMA accounting;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA accounting TO otelu;

-- Accounting Service: create tables
CREATE TABLE accounting."order" (
    order_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY
);

CREATE TABLE accounting.shipping (
    shipping_tracking_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    shipping_cost_currency_code TEXT NOT NULL,
    shipping_cost_units BIGINT NOT NULL,
    shipping_cost_nanos INT NOT NULL,
    street_address TEXT,
    city TEXT,
    state TEXT,
    country TEXT,
    zip_code TEXT,
    order_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES accounting."order"(order_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE accounting.orderitem (
    item_cost_currency_code TEXT NOT NULL,
    item_cost_units BIGINT NOT NULL,
    item_cost_nanos INT NOT NULL,
    product_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    quantity INT NOT NULL,
    order_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES accounting."order"(order_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- Accounting Service: grant permission to schema
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA accounting TO otelu;

-- Product Review Service: create a schema
CREATE SCHEMA reviews;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA reviews TO otelu;

-- Product Review Service: create tables
CREATE TABLE reviews.productreviews (
    id INTEGER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
    username VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    description VARCHAR(1024),
    score NUMERIC(2,1) NOT NULL
);

-- Product Review Service: create index for product_id lookups

-- Product Review Service: grant permission to schema
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA reviews TO otelu;
